# About this course reader {.unnumbered}

This site is the written version of the whole of **Emne 1 - Cybersecurity,
networks, Linux and scripting** at Gokstad Akademiet: one chapter for each of
the twenty-six lectures, in full sentences, with the book references beside
every claim. It says the same things as the slides and the afternoon
sessions, in a form you can read before and after each lecture.

**How to read it.** Each chapter opens with a metadata box naming its module,
lecture and reading time. The coloured boxes follow one convention
throughout:

::: {.callout-note}
## Definition
Blue **note** boxes are definitions taken from the book, quoted with their
source.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you read on
Orange **warning** boxes are questions to stop and answer for yourself.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Nordvik AS
Green **case** boxes follow one small firm, Nordvik AS, through the whole
semester.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Key idea
Red **key-idea** boxes are the ideas to keep.
:::

Each chapter ends with common misconceptions, a five-point summary, a
self-check, and the sources used.

**Light and dark.** Every page has a light/dark toggle in the top right
corner - pick whichever is easier on your eyes; the choice is remembered
across pages.

**Books.** Jøsang, *Cybersecurity: Technology and Governance* (Springer,
2025) for Modules 1–3; Horstmann & Necaise, *Python for Everyone* (3rd ed.)
for the Python chapters. Linux, Bash and web facts are attributed where they
are used.

## The four modules {.unnumbered}

| Module | Chapters | Covers |
|:-----------------------|:---------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 - Foundations | 1–4 | The field, digital systems, risk, and the law |
| 2 - Networking | 5–10 | Networks, addresses, ports, segmentation, routing, wireless |
| 3 - Linux / SecOps | 11–14 | The terminal, logs, users and permissions, services and hardening |
| 4 - Scripting | 15–26 | Python, files, databases, Bash, and the web |
